notes: acceptable_verdicts is a list, not a single value: any verdict in it counts as correct for this topic_id.

A null acceptable_verdicts marks a topic this file does not score for verdict accuracy: sdvosb_certification_status, subcontracting_cap_representation, quote_due_date, and quote_submission_channel, since all four are is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json.

rfq_completeness_signature accepts both compliant and insufficient_information: a first real pipeline run flagged this as a mismatch (predicted insufficient_information, reasoning that the application's cover-letter claim of a signed/dated RFQ is not the same as seeing an actual completed RFQ form) -- a defensible reading given the application never reproduces a filled-in SF-1449-style form, only asserts completeness and shows a separate Volume IV signature block, so both readings are accepted rather than treating the model's skepticism as wrong.

The application deliberately varies its error types: compliant (7 topics), non_compliant across different shapes -- a disclosure omitted entirely (GWAC/MAS status) and a deliverable deferred past the proposal deadline (PPQ) -- insufficient_information for two partial-coverage shapes (floor restoration addressing only one of three elements; field service report addressing only two of five elements) plus one under-specified compliance claim (PPE mentioned but the specific OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard elements never addressed), and one contradictory claim (the lead FSE's experience and certification status stated two incompatible ways).
description is copied verbatim from the matching topic_id in true_requirements.json so this file can be read alone; true_requirements.json is the source of truth if the two diverge.

verdicts.description: The RFQ response must be completed in its entirety and be signed and dated; an incomplete, unsigned, or undated response will not be considered for award.
verdicts.rationale: Application states the RFQ is submitted complete and signed/dated, and includes an actual signature block with a filled-in date.

evidence.quote:
This RFQ is submitted complete in its entirety, signed
and dated below by our authorized representative.

verdicts.description: To be eligible for this 100% SDVOSB set-aside, the offeror's service-disabled veteran-owned small business status must be verified and visible in the SBA Small Business Certification database both at the time of quote submission and at award.
verdicts.rationale: is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json -- actual SBA certification database status cannot be confirmed by reading the application text, only by checking the database directly.

verdicts.description: Offeror must state whether the quoted items are available and priced through an existing Government-wide Acquisition Contract (GWAC), GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS), or VA-wide Acquisition Contract.
verdicts.rationale: Application never states whether the quoted items are available and priced through a GWAC, GSA MAS, or VA-wide Acquisition Contract -- the disclosure is omitted entirely.

verdicts.description: Volume I must demonstrate how the offeror's quote meets the Statement of Work and solicitation requirements, including testing plans, lab certifications, and alignment with the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP).
verdicts.rationale: Application includes a Volume I narrative explicitly framed as demonstrating how the quote meets the SOW and solicitation requirements, addressing the SOW task sequence and QASP.

evidence.quote:
Summit Biomedical Field Services demonstrates the following approach to meeting the
requirements of the Statement of Work (SOW) and this solicitation, addressing the SOW
task sequence directly, section by section, and consistent with the Quality Assurance
Surveillance Plan.

verdicts.description: The technical approach must establish and maintain an Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) Level IV compliant work area around the Radiology room -- dust barriers and protective measures as directed by facility Infection Prevention/Safety staff, plus debris control, cleaning, and containment throughout the work.
verdicts.rationale: Application commits to establishing and maintaining an ICRA Level IV compliant work area with dust barriers, facility-directed protective measures, and continuous debris control/cleaning/containment.

evidence.quote:
Infection Control: Summit will establish and maintain a full Infection Control Risk
Assessment (ICRA) Level IV compliant work area surrounding the Radiology suite for the
duration of the project, including dust barriers and any protective measures directed by
the facility's Infection Prevention and/or Safety offices, and will implement continuous
debris control, cleaning, and containment measures throughout de-installation and
removal.

verdicts.description: The technical approach must address removing anchoring bolts/hardware from the floor, restoring the floor to a flush condition suitable for future construction, and removing all resulting trash and debris.
verdicts.rationale: Application addresses only the anchoring-bolt removal portion of this requirement and never mentions restoring the floor to a flush condition or removing the resulting trash/debris, so it is unclear whether the full floor-restoration task will be performed.

evidence.quote:
Floor Area: Upon completion of system removal, Summit will remove all anchoring bolts
and other hardware associated with the GE INNOVA 4100-IQ installation from the floor.

verdicts.description: The offeror's approach must account for delivering a detailed field service report upon completion, at minimum covering equipment identification, dates/times on site, description of tasks performed, confirmation of the monitor arm's final disposition, and any issues encountered with corrective actions taken.
verdicts.rationale: Application commits to a field service report covering equipment identification and on-site dates, but never mentions a description of tasks performed, confirmation of the monitor arm's disposition, or issues/corrective actions, so it is unclear whether the full required report content will be provided.

evidence.quote:
Field Service Report: Upon completion of work, Summit will submit a field service report
to Biomedical Engineering and the COR documenting the equipment removed (device name
and model) and the dates of on-site work.

verdicts.description: All Field Service Engineers performing the work must be fully qualified: formally trained (OEM or equivalent) in imaging-system de-installation and related tasks, and with at least two years of field experience maintaining or de-installing comparable imaging systems.
verdicts.rationale: Application states the assigned lead FSE has 5 years of field experience and holds current OEM certification, but later states the same person joined the field service team eight months ago and is still completing OEM certification training -- the two statements cannot both be true.

evidence.quote:
Personnel: The lead Field Service Engineer assigned to this project, Daniel Reyes, has
5 years of hands-on field experience de-installing and maintaining GE imaging systems and
holds current OEM de-installation certification.

Note on personnel assigned above: Mr. Reyes joined Summit's field service team eight
months ago and is currently completing his OEM de-installation certification training,
under the supervision of a senior engineer on all field assignments.

verdicts.description: The contractor's approach must comply with the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard: educating employees on risks, implementing exposure-reduction policies/procedures, providing counseling/treatment mechanisms after potential exposure, and providing/enforcing PPE use.
verdicts.rationale: Application only states that personnel wear PPE in accordance with OSHA requirements generally -- it never addresses employee education on bloodborne pathogen risks, exposure-reduction policies/procedures, or post-exposure counseling/treatment mechanisms, so compliance with the specific OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard elements cannot be confirmed.

evidence.quote:
Safety: Summit's personnel wear appropriate personal protective equipment on all job
sites in accordance with OSHA requirements.

verdicts.description: Offeror must complete the pricing schedule (price the base year line item, plus any option year line items) as part of Volume II.
verdicts.rationale: Application fills in a price for the base-year CLIN and states a matching total price.

evidence.quote:

verdicts.description: Offeror must provide completed Past Performance Questionnaires (PPQ) signed by the point of contact who oversaw performance (or an equal representative), submitted either by the offeror with its proposal or directly by the third party by the proposal deadline.
verdicts.rationale: Application defers submission of the Past Performance Questionnaires to after a notice of intent to award, rather than providing them signed and submitted with the proposal as required.

evidence.quote:
Past Performance Questionnaires for the above references will be provided upon request
following any notice of intent to award.

verdicts.description: Offeror must complete VAAR 852.219-75 VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting -- Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction, as Volume IV of the quote.
verdicts.rationale: Application includes the VAAR 852.219-75 certification language, signed and dated by an authorized representative.

evidence.quote:
Summit Biomedical Field Services, LLC certifies that if awarded the contract, it will
comply with the limitations on subcontracting specified in VAAR 852.219-75 and the
resultant contract.

verdicts.description: Offeror must list any/all subcontractors it will use (with their size standard under NAICS 541380) and what they will perform, and explain how it will comply with the limitations on subcontracting -- or state that no subcontractors will be used.
verdicts.rationale: Application states plainly that no subcontractors will be used, matching the required fallback statement for offerors not using subcontractors.

evidence.quote: No subcontractors will be used for this requirement.

verdicts.description: By certifying compliance with the VAAR 852.219-75 clause for this services acquisition, the offeror represents it will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the Government to firms that are not certified SDVOSBs/VOSBs.
verdicts.rationale: is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json -- actual compliance with the 50% subcontracting cap cannot be confirmed by reading the application, only by auditing subcontract payments during performance.

verdicts.description: Quotes are due to the Contract Specialist by 10:00 AM MT, July 7, 2026.
verdicts.rationale: is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json -- the due date is a fact about the submission process, not something the application's content addresses.

verdicts.description: Quotes must be submitted by email only (4MB limit); hand-carried and faxed quotes are not accepted.
verdicts.rationale: is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json -- which channel was actually used to submit the quote is a fact about the submission process, not something the application's own content addresses.
